title: NIN Modification Portal: Correct Your NIN Details Online
excerpt: Learn which NIN details can be corrected, the documents to prepare, how submission works, and what to do if a request is delayed or rejected.

sections.content: Your 11-digit National Identification Number is tied to your identity record. If a name, date of birth, phone number, or address is wrong, correct the inaccurate field rather than applying for another NIN. A mismatch can cause verification problems when a bank, telecom provider, school, employer, or government service compares your NIN details with another record.

NIMC lists supported self-service modifications for name, phone number, date of birth, and address. Start with the official NIMC guidance or use a traceable assisted submission service. Ufriends can help prepare, submit, and track a supported request, but NIMC remains responsible for reviewing the evidence and approving any change to the national record.

Before paying, compare the NIN record with the strongest legal document for the field you want to change. Write down the exact old and proposed details, collect consistent evidence, and confirm the current fee and refund terms. Do not change a correct NIN record merely to match an incorrect bank or school record.

This guide separates the tasks visitors often mix together: choosing the correct modification type, preparing documents, submitting the request, interpreting its status, and asking for review when it is returned or rejected.

sections.content: What is NIN Modification on Ufriends IT?

NIN modification on Ufriends IT is an assisted submission service for supported corrections such as name, date of birth, or phone number. Ufriends helps customers prepare, submit, and track a request through its dashboard; NIMC remains the authority that reviews evidence and controls changes to the National Identity Database. Some cases may still require additional verification or an in-person visit.

The online route lets you upload the requested evidence and keep a traceable order reference. It does not guarantee approval or instant synchronisation with banks, telecom providers, or other organisations. Before paying, confirm the supported correction, required documents, displayed fee, expected review process, and refund terms.
The NIN Modification Agreement: What You Must Know
Because identity updates are highly secure, Ufriends IT requires all users to read and accept the NIN Modification Agreement before submitting a request. Here are the key terms you should know:

items: Voluntary authorisation: Submit only your own request, or one you are legally authorised to manage, and review every proposed detail before confirming.
Evidence-based review: Payment does not guarantee approval. The proposed change must agree with the supporting documents and NIMC requirements.
Separate synchronisation: An approved NIN correction may appear in the national record before a bank, telecom provider, or other organisation refreshes its local profile.

sections.content: Required Documents for NIN Modification
To prove that the requested changes are legitimate, you must provide supporting documentation. Collect the relevant documents before starting to prevent processing rejections:

items: For a name change: NIMC lists a court affidavit, newspaper extract, marriage certificate where applicable, and another government-issued ID. Make sure the proposed name is consistent across the evidence.

For a date-of-birth correction: NIMC's self-service guidance requires a digitised NPC birth certificate for people born after 1992 or a digitised NPC attestation certificate for people born before 1992.
For a phone-number modification: NIMC lists a police report. Review the current portal instructions for the required number format and any additional evidence before submitting.

sections.content: The Strict NPC Birth Certificate Rule

For online date-of-birth modification, NIMC says the NPC certificate number must be validated and the resulting date is filled automatically. Its current guidance distinguishes between a digitised NPC attestation certificate for applicants born before 1992 and a digitised NPC birth certificate for applicants born after 1992. Check the official portal before paying because document and fee requirements can change.
Step-by-Step Online NIN Modification Guide on Ufriends IT
Follow these simple steps to submit your NIN modification request online:

steps.title: Open a Free Account
steps.content: Go to Ufriends.com.ng and register a free basic account. The registration is quick and only requires basic details.

steps.title: Fund Your Wallet
steps.content: Use an available funding method shown in your dashboard. Review the displayed charge and wait for the wallet balance to confirm before placing the order; bank-processing time can vary.

steps.title: Navigate to Manual Services
steps.content: Go to the navigation menu on your dashboard, select Manual Services, and click on the NIN Modification tab.

steps.title: Accept the Agreement & Select Type
steps.content: Read and accept the NIN Modification Agreement. Select your modification type (e.g. Change of Name, Arrangement of Name, Correction of DOB, or Change of Phone Number) and enter your 11-digit NIN.

steps.title: Upload and Submit Your Request
steps.content: Type in your old and new details. Upload clear photos of your supporting documents (such as your court affidavit, marriage certificate, or wrong NIN slip).

steps.title: Enter PIN and Submit
steps.content: Review details, agree to the Terms of Service & Privacy Policy, and click Submit. Input your secure 4-digit transaction PIN to authorize the payment deduction.

sections.content: Official Self-Service and Enrolment-Centre Options

You can also use NIMC's official self-service route or visit an enrolment centre when the online or assisted process does not fit your case. Check NIMC's current requirements and fees before travelling because document rules and service charges can change. Bring the original supporting evidence and keep the payment and transaction references issued for the request.
What Happens After Submission?

After submission, use the order history to check whether the request is awaiting documents, under review, completed, returned, or rejected. Processing time varies by correction type, document validation, portal availability, and whether NIMC requests another step. Treat any estimate as guidance rather than a guarantee.
How Long Does NIN Modification Take?

NIMC's centre-based guidance says a completed modification may take 2–5 working days or longer depending on network and backend availability. Online and assisted requests can follow a different review path, especially for date-of-birth changes that require an NPC certificate or attestation. Count from the date the documents became complete, not merely from the first payment attempt.

items: Submitted means the request was recorded; it does not mean approved.
Under review means the evidence is still being checked.
Returned means a clearer document or corrected entry may be required.
Approved means you should obtain a fresh NIN slip and verify the changed field.
If another organisation still shows old data, ask it to revalidate the updated NIN record.

sections.content: Rejected NIN Modifications and Refunds

A request can be rejected when the proposed detail conflicts with the supporting evidence, a document is unreadable or cannot be verified, the wrong modification type was selected, or the requested field is not updatable. Save the payment receipt, transaction reference, uploaded document names, and complete rejection message before contacting support.

Do not assume every rejected request is refundable. NIMC's published adult-modification guidance describes the date-of-birth processing fee as non-refundable. Other cases depend on whether the issue was a duplicate debit, an unattached payment, an assisted-service fee, or a completed review that ended in rejection. Ask support to identify the transaction type before paying again.
Checking Your NIN Verification Status

After NIMC marks the request approved, obtain a fresh NIN slip through an available official or assisted route and compare the corrected field carefully. The NIMC mobile identity service can also display refreshed profile information where available. If another organisation still shows the old detail, give it the updated record and ask it to revalidate your NIN; do not assume every connected profile refreshes automatically.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
To prevent rejections, avoid these common mistakes when modifying your NIN details:

items: Paying unverified agents: Do not send identity documents, passwords, or OTPs through social-media direct messages. Use NIMC's official route or a traceable assisted service with a receipt and support record.
Duplicate enrolment: Never attempt to register for a second NIN to fix an error. NIMC identifies the NIN itself as a non-updatable field; correct the supported detail attached to the existing number.

Mismatched document details: Ensure the proposed name is consistent across the affidavit, newspaper extract, marriage certificate where applicable, and supporting ID. An unexplained mismatch can delay the review or lead to a returned request.
Uploading Dark or Blurry Documents: Automated scanners and human validators reject unreadable files. Ensure you capture clear, well-lit images of your affidavits and certificates.

sections.content: Why Choose Ufriends IT for Your Identity Needs?

Ufriends is useful when you want a guided submission, one dashboard for the order, and a traceable support reference. It does not replace NIMC or guarantee approval. The service is most suitable when you already know the incorrect field and have consistent supporting evidence. If only the name is wrong, use the focused NIN name-correction checklist. If the issue is a BVN and NIN mismatch, compare both records before deciding which one to correct.

items: Check requirements first: Review the correction type and required documents before funding the request.
See the live price: Sign in and confirm the displayed service price instead of relying on an old article or screenshot.
Submit through your dashboard: Keep sensitive information inside the authenticated workflow rather than a public chat.
Track one reference: Use the order history and official support channel for status questions.
Verify the result: After approval, obtain a fresh NIN slip and ask affected organisations to revalidate it.

sections.content: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

items: Can I modify my NIN details online? NIMC provides self-service modification for supported fields. Ufriends also provides an assisted submission route; approval remains subject to NIMC review.
How long does a correction take? Time varies by request and evidence. NIMC's centre guidance gives 2–5 working days or longer, while online cases may differ.
How much does Ufriends charge? Check the live price in the authenticated service before submitting because prices and requirements can change.
Why was my request rejected? Common causes include inconsistent details, an unreadable upload, an invalid supporting document, or selection of the wrong correction type.
Will I receive a refund? It depends on the transaction and applicable terms. NIMC describes its date-of-birth processing fee as non-refundable; contact support before paying again.
How do I confirm approval? Obtain a fresh NIN slip and compare the corrected field. If another organisation still has old information, ask it to revalidate the NIN.
Will banks update automatically? Not always. A bank may need to refresh its local customer profile after the central NIN record changes.
Should I create another NIN? No. Correct supported details on the existing record; do not attempt duplicate enrolment.
